intro: Bhutan, the 'Land of the Thunder Dragon', is a Himalayan Buddhist kingdom that stayed independent and isolated for centuries and measures success by Gross National Happiness.

chapters.title: Buddhism arrives
text: Buddhism came to Bhutan in the 600s and 700s. Guru Rinpoche, a revered teacher, is said to have flown to the cliff where Taktsang, the Tiger's Nest monastery, now stands.

chapters.title: Zhabdrung and the dzongs
text: In 1616 a Tibetan lama, Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal, arrived and united Bhutan. He built dzongs, huge fortress-monasteries that still serve as centres of religion and government, and fought off Tibetan invasions.

chapters.title: Kings and democracy
text: In 1907 Ugyen Wangchuck became the first hereditary king. Bhutan kept itself closed to outsiders; television and the internet only arrived in 1999.
In 2008 the fourth king gave up absolute power and Bhutan became a constitutional monarchy with elections. In the 1990s many Nepali-speaking Lhotshampa people were forced to leave.

highlight.title: Happiness
highlight.text: The fourth king said Gross National Happiness matters more than Gross National Product.

keyTerms.meaning: Bhutan's way of measuring progress by well-being.
